return_hassle.text:
At present, I no longer consider Myntra a trustworthy shopping platform based on my experience. Customers may receive incomplete, incorrect, or entirely different products from what they ordered, and even when valid return requests are raised with supporting evidence, they can face unnecessary rejection or delays.
In my experience, the situation becomes even more frustrating when the logistics partner allegedly makes no genuine attempt to collect the return, yet the return is marked as cancelled or failed based on the pickup agent’s own status update. What is even more concerning is the suspension or deactivation of a customer’s account while valid returns, refunds, and the customer’s money remain unresolved. This leaves customers feeling helpless and raises serious concerns about the transparency and accountability of the platform’s return, logistics, and account-management processes. Myntra should prioritize customer protection, transparent investigations, genuine pickup attempts, timely refunds, and fair treatment instead of leaving customers to struggle to recover money for products they did not receive correctly. New Income source of income for Myntra...😒

other.text:
>>You need the product tomorrow?

If you are in a metro then you get the item shipped next day. I've shopped with Flipkart, Myntra etc and this has always been the norm and when usually it becomes 2-3 days it's because your stuff is being sent from a warehouse in another metro. As I live in B'lore Myntra has almost always done 1-day shipping or 2 at most.

You want your items to be shipped to a small town? There's a problem. You want to ship it to your parents in a very small town or rural area? Forget it!

There are other services like eBay India, which has recently, started 3-4 day shipping. Earlier for them it was 7-8 minimum as standard. Deal sites like SnapDeal etc follow the same minimum 7-8 days golden rule.

Sites like IndiaPlaza are plague. You get your stuff in months or fortnights and then you congratulate yourself.

The thing is there are so many options in India, even on smaller scales, for online shopping and people actively use them where they best deals. In USA when I try to buy sth, to get it via a friend who is coming form USA, I have more or less one option - Amazon!
other.blocker_detail: shipping not available to small towns or rural areas causing delays

quality_doubt.text:
Online shopping is 90% guessing, 10% hoping you didn’t just buy trash
I try to be intentional when I shop—buy things that are sustainable, safe, ethical, actually *worth* the money—but let’s be honest: online shopping makes that nearly impossible.

Every product is “eco,” “clean,” “non-toxic,” “handcrafted,” “minimalist,” or some other buzzword. Until it arrives in five layers of plastic, smells weird, and breaks in two weeks.

I’m tired of:  
❌ Fake reviews  
❌ Greenwashed branding  
❌ $40 “clean” products that are just scented nonsense  
❌ Buying stuff that becomes clutter 2 months later

There should be a browser extension or app that gives you a *real* read on a product *while* you shop:  
⚠️ This is overpriced garbage  
✅ This is legit and built to last  
🧪 This contains stuff you might want to avoid  
🌍 Bonus points if it’s ethical and low-impact

Until that exists, I’ll just keep reading 47 reviews and hoping I don’t regret it.

What’s the worst thing you’ve ever bought online that *seemed* great?
quality_doubt.blocker_detail: concern over misleading product claims and low durability
